content.title: How can a good God allow suffering?
content.summary: God is sovereign and good; evil is real, and Christ is our hope.

answer.text: God governs all things without becoming the author of sin. Scripture never asks us to call evil good. It shows him bringing good through what creatures intend for evil, supremely at Christ's cross. We know his character and promises without knowing his hidden purpose in every loss.

reasoning.text: Joseph names his brothers' intention as evil and God's intention in the same events as good.
Jesus was delivered according to God's purpose, yet those who crucified him acted wickedly.
For those who love God, suffering cannot defeat his purpose of conforming them to Christ.

conclusion.text: Our hope rests in God's sovereign goodness and the risen Christ, not in pretending we can explain every tragedy.

sections.text: A reply that treats suffering as outside God's government fails to express the Reformed confession. Scripture holds together divine purpose and creaturely responsibility. It does not portray God as helpless before human decisions or blind natural forces.
sections.title: More than a free-will answer

sections.text: Jesus weeps at Lazarus's tomb. The Psalms give words for anguish. When someone is grieving, listening and weeping with them may be the first faithful response. God's promises do not require them to disguise pain.
sections.title: Lament belongs to faith

content.objection: Does a good purpose make evil acceptable?

reply.text: No. The brothers' evil remained evil, and the crucifixion involved guilty human action. God's power to redeem suffering does not authorise us to inflict, conceal or excuse it.

limit.text: Romans 8:28 is a promise to those who love God, not a claim that every event feels good. Do not announce the secret reason for someone's loss as if God had revealed it to you.

citations.locator: The recipients and meaning of the promise

prompt.text: Would it help more to discuss the question now, or to have someone listen and grieve with you?

passages.note: Human evil and God's good purpose
